You are prepared to hear from me the *Nāmasamgīti*, which is of great significance, purifying, and a thunderbolt that destroys evil, belonging to Mañjuśrī’s body of gnosis.
"Therefore, O Lord of Guhyakas, I shall teach it well to you; listen with a one-pointed mind. "Very well, Blessed One," he replied.
There are six verses of response.
Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, having surveyed the entire great family of mantras, the family of mantra-vidyādharas, and the three families, [proceeded].
The worldly and supramundane family, the great family that illuminates the world, the supreme family of Mahāmudrā, and the great family of the Great Uṣṇīṣa.
Two verses on the contemplation of the six families.
The Lord of Speech spoke this verse, which is endowed with the six kings of mantras, the arising of non-duality, and the nature of non-arising.
A, Ā, I, Ī, U, Ū, E, AI, O, AU, Aṃ, Aḥ—abiding in the heart, I am the embodiment of wisdom, the awakened one among the Buddhas who dwell in the three times.
Oṃ! Homage to you, O Vajratīkṣṇa, the embodiment of the wisdom-knowledge that cuts through suffering, the Lord of Speech, the Knowledge-Body, Arapacana.
Three verses on the sequence of awakening through the net of illusion.

For example: "The Blessed One, the Buddha, the Perfectly Awakened One, is born from the syllable *A*; the syllable *A* is the foremost of all letters, of great significance, and the supreme syllable."
For it is the Great Breath, unborn and devoid of verbal expression; the foremost cause of all speech, it is the perfect radiance of all words.
The great, great, great passion who brings delight to all sentient beings; the great, great, great hatred who is the great enemy of all afflictions.
The great festival, the great delusion, the destroyer of the delusion of the dull-witted; the great festival, the great wrath, the great enemy of wrath, the Great One.
The great festival, the great greed, the destroyer of all greed; the great desire, the great bliss, the great joy, and the great delight.
He has a great form, a great body, a great color, and a great physique; he has a great name, is most noble, and possesses a vast and expansive mandala.
He who wields the great weapon of wisdom, the foremost leader with the great goad against the afflictions; he of great renown, great fame, great light, and great splendor.
The wise one who possesses the great illusion, the accomplisher of the purpose of the great illusion, who delights in the pleasure of the great illusion, and the master of the great illusory net.
The most excellent great lord of donors, the foremost upholder of great morality, the steadfast upholder of great patience, and one whose prowess is great vigor.
Abiding in the samādhi of great meditative concentration, bearing the body of great wisdom, possessing great power and great skillful means, he is an ocean of the knowledge of his vows.
Consisting of great loving-kindness, immeasurable, possessing great compassion, supreme in resolve, of great wisdom, of great intelligence, possessing great skillful means, and of great action.
Endowed with the power of great supernatural faculties, possessing great momentum and great speed; possessed of great miraculous power, of great renown, and of great strength and prowess.
The shatterer of the great mountain of existence, the dense Great Vajra-holder; the greatly fierce, the greatly terrible, the one who causes fear even to the fearful.
The Lord is the supreme among great vidyās; the Guru is the supreme among great mantras. He has ascended the path of the Mahāyāna and is the highest of the Mahāyāna systems.
The fourteen verses of the Great Mandala of the Vajra Realm.
Buddha Mahāvairocana is the great observer of silence, the great sage; he has arisen from the Great Mantra Method and is the very essence of the Great Mantra Method.
He has attained the ten perfections; he is the locus of the ten perfections; he is the purity of the ten perfections; he is the method of the ten perfections.
The Lord is the master of the ten stages, established upon the ten stages; his self is purified by the ten knowledges, and he maintains the purity of the ten knowledges.

The Lord of Sages possesses ten aspects and is the goal of ten meanings; he is the All-Pervading One endowed with the ten powers. He accomplishes the welfare of the entire universe without exception, the Great One who has mastery over the ten aspects.
He is beginningless, of a nature free from conceptual proliferation, a pure self, and whose essence is suchness; he speaks the truth, acts according to his word, and his speech is never otherwise.
Non-dual and proponent of non-duality, established in the limit of reality, he utters the lion’s roar of selflessness, putting to flight the deer of false teachers.
All-pervading, his movement never in vain, possessing the speed of the mind of a Tathāgata; the Victor who has conquered his enemies, the triumphant universal monarch of great power.

He is the leader of the host, the teacher of the host, the lord of the host, the master of the host, the self-controlled one; he is of great majesty, the preeminent leader, not led by others, and the one of the great method.
Lord of speech, master of speech, eloquent, lord of words, one whose utterances are infinite; speaker of truth, truthful speaker, and teacher of the Four Truths.
For he is irreversible, a non-returner, a rhinoceros-like solitary leader; having emerged through various modes of deliverance, he is the single cause of the great elements.
The Arhat, the monk whose taints are exhausted, free from passion, with senses conquered, has attained security and reached fearlessness; he is indeed cooled and undisturbed.
Endowed with perfect knowledge and conduct, the Sugata, the supreme knower of the world,
free from the notions of "mine" and "I," abides in the principle of the two truths.
Standing on the far shore of saṃsāra, having accomplished what was to be done, he stands on firm ground;
having spat out the knowledge of absolute liberation, he is the destroyer who wields the weapon of wisdom.
The True Dharma is the King of Dharma, radiant, the supreme illuminator of the world;
it is the Lord of Dharma, the Sovereign of Dharma, and the teacher of the path to the highest good.
Siddhārtha, whose resolve is accomplished and who is free from all conceptual constructions,
is the non-conceptual, inexhaustible realm, the supreme and imperishable dharmadhātu.
He possesses merit, the accumulation of merit; he is wisdom, the great source of wisdom.
He possesses wisdom, knowing both the existent and the non-existent, and is fully endowed with the two accumulations.

Eternal, the sovereign of the universe, the yogin, meditation, the object of meditation, and the lord of the intellects; indeed, he is to be realized within oneself, immovable, the supreme primordial one, the sustainer of the three bodies.
The Buddha is the embodiment of the five bodies, the all-pervading lord whose nature is the five wisdoms;
he has the five Buddhas as his crown, possesses the five eyes, and holds them without attachment.
The progenitor of all Buddhas, the supreme and most excellent Son of the Buddha,
he is born from the source of wisdom, unborn, the source of the Dharma, and the bringer of an end to existence.
The solid essence, the diamond-natured one, the newly born Lord of the World,
arisen from space, the self-existent, the great fire of the wisdom of insight.
Vairocana is the great radiance; Virocana is the light of gnosis; he is the lamp of the world, the torch of wisdom, the one of great splendor, and the luminous one.
King of Vidyās, supreme mantra-king, who accomplishes the great purpose;
Great Uṣṇīṣa, wondrous Uṣṇīṣa, the all-seeing Lord of the Sky.
The foremost embodiment of all Buddhas, whose eyes bring joy to the world,
the creator of manifold forms, the one to be worshipped and honored— the Great Sage.
The mantra-practitioner upholds the three families and maintains the mantras of the great samaya;
he is the preeminent bearer of the Three Jewels and the supreme teacher of the three vehicles.
Amoghapāśa, the Victorious One, Vajrapāśa, the Great Seizer;
Vajrāṅkuśa, the Great Noose—these are twenty-four and a quarter verses on the knowledge of the perfectly pure dharmadhātu.
The terrifying one who strikes fear with the vajra.
(66) Krodharāja, the six-faced, the formidable, the six-eyed, the six-armed, the mighty;
the Skeleton with fangs terrifying to behold, who possesses a hundred faces like the Halāhala poison.
Yamāntaka, Vighnarāja, Vajravega, Bhayaṃkara,
Vighuṣṭavajra, Hṛdvajra, Māyāvajra, and Mahodara.
The Lord of the Thunderbolt, whose source is the Vajra, is the Vajra-maṇḍala, resembling the sky;
he has the fierce power of a single matted lock that is immovable, and he wears a fresh garment of elephant hide.
The cry of "Hā! Hā! is most terrible; the sound of "Hi!
Hi! is fearsome; the loud laugh, the great laugh, the diamond-like laugh, and the great roar.
Vajrasattva, the Great Being; Vajrarāja, the Great Bliss; Vajracaṇḍa, the Great Joy; Vajra-hūṃkāra, the Utterer of Hūṃ.
(71) He who bears the weapon of the vajra-arrow, the vajra-sword that cuts through,
the bearer of the universal vajra, the wielder of the vajra, the sole vajra-holder, who abandons all conflict.
(72) His eyes are formidable with vajra-flames; his hair is vajra-flames.
He is the vajra-penetration, the great penetration, the hundred-eyed one, and the vajra-eyed one.
His body is covered with hair-tips like vajras; his entire form consists of vajra-hair;
he has the onset of vajra-pointed nails; and his skin is as dense as the essence of the vajra.
The glorious one who wears a garland of vajras, adorned with vajra ornaments;
he whose roar is the "ha-ha" and "aṭṭa-hāsa" laughter, the sound of the vajra, the six-syllabled one.
(75) Of lovely voice and great roar, the single great sound of the three worlds;
his resonance extends to the limits of the realm of space, he who is the best among those possessed of voice.
(76) Verses on the Mirror-like Wisdom: twelve and three-quarters.
Suchness, true selflessness, the limit of reality, and the ineffable;
the bull among proponents of emptiness, whose roar is profound and vast.
The great-sounding conch of Dharma, the great drum of Dharma,
the nirvana of non-abiding, and the drum of Dharma resounding through the ten directions.
(78) Formless yet possessing form, the foremost, manifold in form and made of mind;
the glory that illuminates all forms, the bearer of every reflection without exception.
Invincible, of great renown, the Great Lord of the triple world;
established upon the exalted Noble Path, the Banner of Dharma, of great prosperity.
(80) With the body of the sole prince of the three worlds, he is ancient, aged, and the Lord of Creatures;
bearing the thirty-two marks, he is beloved and the most beautiful in the three worlds.
(81) A teacher of the qualities of worldly knowledge, a teacher of the world, and one who is self-confident;
a protector, a savior, the friend of the three worlds, a refuge, a deliverer, and unsurpassed.
(82) He enjoys the vast expanse of the sky; he is an ocean of the wisdom of the Omniscient One;
he is the shatterer of the shell of the egg of ignorance and the breaker of the cage of existence.
(83) With all afflictions completely pacified, having reached the further shore of the ocean of saṃsāra,
crowned with the consecration of primordial wisdom, he is adorned as a perfectly awakened Buddha.
(84) He is the pacifier of the suffering of the three types of suffering, the one who has reached the end, the infinite, the one who has attained the three liberations;
he is completely freed from all obscurations and has reached equality with space.
(85) Transcending the stains of all afflictions, having gone beyond the path of the three times;
the great elephant among all beings, the crest-jewel upon the crest of all virtues.
(86) Completely liberated from all substrates, well-established on the path of space,
the all-pervading Lord is the bearer of the great wish-fulfilling gem, the supreme among all jewels.
He is a flourishing great wish-fulfilling tree, a supreme and most auspicious vessel;
he is the performer of the welfare of all beings, a benefactor who desires their well-being and is affectionate toward sentient beings.

(88) He knows the auspicious and the inauspicious; he knows the [right] time, he knows the occasion, he is observant of the commitments, and all-pervading. He knows the faculties of sentient beings, he knows the proper moment, and he is skilled in the three liberations.
(89) He is possessed of virtues, a knower of virtues, a knower of the Dharma, praised, the source of auspiciousness;
he is the most auspicious of all auspicious things, glory, fortune, fame, and purity. (90)
He is the great festival, the great relief, the great bliss, and the great delight;
he is honor, hospitality, prosperity, joy, fortune, and the lord of glory.
(91) The one to be chosen, the giver of boons, the most excellent, the worthy refuge, the supreme protector,
the enemy of great fear, the preeminent one, the destroyer of every last trace of fear.
(92) He who has a crest, a tuft of hair, matted locks, a shaven head, or a diadem; he who is five-faced, five-crested, and has five locks of hair as his crown.
(93) A bearer of the great vows, wearing the girdle of muñja grass, a celibate student, supreme in his observances,
a great ascetic, devoted to austerity, a bath-graduate, Gautama was the foremost.
The knower of Brahman is a Brāhmaṇa; he has attained Brahman and the nirvāṇa of Brahman.
He is liberation, release, the limb of liberation, emancipation, tranquility, and the auspicious.
(95) Nirvana, extinction, peace, the highest good, departure, the end; the ender of pleasure and pain, the ultimate goal, dispassion, and the destruction of the substrata.
(96) Unconquered, incomparable, manifest, without appearance, stainless, partless, all-pervading, omnipresent, subtle, the seed, and untainted.
(97) Free from dust, stainless, immaculate, having cast out faults, and free from disease; perfectly awakened, with a self fully enlightened, the omniscient, the all-knowing, the supreme.
(98) Transcending the nature of consciousness, wisdom maintains a non-dual form; it is free from conceptual construction, effortless, and performs the activities of the Buddhas of the three times.
The Buddha is without beginning or end, the primordial Buddha, without causal lineage;
he is the stainless single eye of gnosis, the embodiment of gnosis, the Tathāgata.
Master of speech, great debater, king of debaters, bull among debaters;
the best of those who speak, the most excellent, the lion of speakers, unconquered.
(101) Samantadarśin, Prāmodya, Tejomālin, Sudarśana, Śrīvatsa, Suprabha, Dipti, Bhā, and Bhāsurakaradyuti.
The supreme and most excellent great physician, the peerless remover of the arrow [of suffering], the tree of all medicinal herbs without exception, the great enemy of the disease of the afflictions.
The beloved Tilaka of the three worlds, the illustrious Mandala of the stars, reaching to the limits of the sky in the ten directions, he is the great, lofty banner of the Dharma.
The sole vast umbrella of the world, the mandala of loving-kindness and compassion, the glorious Padmanarteśvara, the great all-pervading Lord Ratnacchatra.
The great king of all Buddhas, who maintains the embodiment of all Buddhas; the great yoga of all Buddhas, the sole teaching of all Buddhas.
The glorious one consecrated with the vajra-jewel, the sovereign lord of all jewels, the lord of all lords of the world, the supreme master of all vajra-holders.
The great mind of all Buddhas, the one who reaches the minds of all Buddhas, the great body of all Buddhas, and the eloquence of all Buddhas.
The great light of the Vajra-Sun, possessing the stainless radiance of the Vajra-Moon; the great passion beginning with dispassion, blazing with light of every color.

The Perfectly Awakened One, seated in the vajra posture, upholder of the Dharma of the Buddha-assembly; the glorious one born from the lotus of the Buddhas, upholder of the treasury of omniscient wisdom.
The King who wields the universal illusion, the great master of the Buddhas' vidyā; the Vajra-Sharp One, the Great Sword, the utterly pure, the supreme syllable.
The Great Vehicle that cuts through suffering, the great weapon of Vajradharma; Jinajik, profound as a vajra, Vajrabuddhi, the knower of things as they truly are.
He who fulfills all the perfections, who adorns all the stages, whose heart radiates light like the moon of perfect wisdom, and who possesses the purity of the selflessness of phenomena.
The Great Exertion of the Net of Illusion, the supreme sovereign of all tantras; he who sits in the vajra posture without exception, the bearer of the entire body of gnosis.
Samantabhadra, Sumati, Kṣitigarbha, Jagaddhṛti, Sarvabuddhamahāgarbha, and Viśvanirmāṇacakradhṛk.

The supreme essence of the nature of all phenomena, the sustainer of the nature of all phenomena; he whose nature is non-arising, who exists for the sake of the universe, and who sustains the nature of all dharmas.

Possessing great wisdom in a single moment, he maintains the awakening to all phenomena; he is the realization of all phenomena, the Sage who has reached the limit of reality, and the one of supreme intellect.
Stable, with a perfectly serene mind, he upholds the awakening of a Samyaksambuddha; he is manifest before all Buddhas, a flame of wisdom, most brilliantly radiant.
The forty-two verses on the wisdom of discernment:
He is the supreme accomplisher of desired aims, the purifier of all miserable states, the Lord who is the highest of all sentient beings, and the liberator of all sentient beings.

The sole hero in the battle against the afflictions, the destroyer of the pride of the enemy that is ignorance; he who possesses wisdom, the glorious one who assumes the forms of the heroic and the loathsome.
He casts down hundreds of many staffs, dancing with every step he takes; possessing the majestic expanse of a hundred arms, he dances across the vast expanse of the sky.
He stands with the entire circle of the earth beneath the sole of one foot, and he stands with the tip of the big toe and its nail resting upon the summit of the Brahmāṇḍa.

The single meaning is the meaning of non-dual phenomena; it is the ultimate reality, indestructible. The object consisting of various representations and forms is the continuity of mind and consciousness.

Delighting in the meaning of all phenomena without exception, he delights in emptiness and possesses supreme intelligence; transcending passion for existence and the like, he finds great delight in the three realms of existence.
White as a pure, bright cloud, with the beautiful luster of the autumn moon’s rays; possessing the brilliance of the orb of the rising sun, and the radiance of great red jewels on his nails.
With a sublime head like the finest sapphire and bearing hair-tips of great blue hue, he possesses the splendor of the radiance of great jewels and is adorned with the emanations of the Buddhas.

He causes a hundred world-systems to tremble, possessing the great stride of the bases of miraculous power; he is the bearer of great mindfulness, the reality itself, and the sovereign of the fourfold mindfulness and meditative concentration.
Mukherji— overwhelmed by the circle of heroes, overwhelmed by the peak;
overwhelmed by the peak, [the] destruction.
Vīra alone reports:
Vinesvara is greedy for sexual pleasure and is pure.

The fragrance of the flowers of the factors of enlightenment, an ocean of the qualities of the Tathāgatas, one who knows the method of the eightfold path, and one who knows the path of the perfectly awakened Buddha.
He is deeply attached to all sentient beings yet free from attachment, like the sky; he is born from the minds of all sentient beings and possesses the speed of the minds of all sentient beings.

He knows the faculties and objects of all sentient beings; he captivates the minds of all sentient beings. He knows the reality of the meaning of the five aggregates; he maintains the purity of the five aggregates.
Abiding at the limit of all deliverance, skilled in all deliverance; abiding on the path of all deliverance, the teacher of all deliverance.
Uprooted from the twelvefold existence, he maintains the purity of the twelve aspects; he possesses the form of the method of the four truths and maintains the realization of the eight knowledges.

He who possesses the meaning of the truths in twelve aspects, who knows reality in sixteen aspects, and who has attained awakening in twenty aspects—the fully awakened one, the supreme omniscient one.
He manifests millions of immeasurable emanation bodies of the Buddha; he is the realization of all moments and knows the meaning of every moment of mind.
He manifests the welfare of the world through the various methods and means of the diverse vehicles; having emerged from the three vehicles, he abides in the fruit of the single vehicle.
His self is purified of the realm of afflictions; he brings about the exhaustion of the realm of karma; he has crossed over the ocean of the floods and emerged from the wilderness of yoga.

Having completely abandoned the afflictions, secondary afflictions, and all defilements along with their habitual tendencies, he performs the welfare of the world unceasingly through wisdom, skillful means, and great compassion.

He whose purpose is the abandonment of all conceptualizations, whose purpose is consciousness, who maintains cessation; he whose domain is the minds of all sentient beings, and who moves within the minds of all sentient beings.
Dwelling within the minds of all sentient beings, having attained equality with their minds, he gladdens the minds of all sentient beings and brings delight to the minds of all sentient beings.

The established doctrine is free from delusion, devoid of all error, characterized by an intellect beyond doubt, possessing three meanings, encompassing all objects, and consisting of the three qualities.
The meaning of the five aggregates, existing in the three times, he is the one who discerns every moment; awakened in a single instant, he upholds the essential nature of all Buddhas.
The bodyless body, the supreme body, the one who manifests the pinnacle of bodies; the great jewel, the crest-jewel of gems, who displays all forms without exception.
The ocean of awakening;
traversed by the mind.
— emanation;
— the yoga of the pure self and karma.
Having gone forth,
he possesses great compassion; it is for the purpose of abandoning that which is not in vain.
He whose course of mind is that of all Buddhas;
he who dwells within;
he who has shaken off the extremes.
—ending in non-delusion;
free from delusion; having arrived at freedom from delusion.
The three times (*trikālaḥ*).
The three periods (*triskālaḥ*).
The three times for the sake of the goal;
the supreme body beyond the limbs of the body;
and the twenty-four verses on the knowledge of equality.
He is to be realized by all the perfectly awakened Buddhas; he is the unsurpassed awakening of the Buddhas. He is without syllables, the source of mantra, and the three great mantra families.

(143) He is the progenitor of the meaning of all mantras, the great bindu, and without syllables. He is the five-syllabled one, the great emptiness, the bindu-emptiness, and the hundred-syllabled one.
(144) He possesses all forms yet is formless; he perceives the half of the half of sixteen bindus. He is partless, beyond calculation, and holds the pinnacle of the fourth dhyāna.
(145) Master of the arts of all meditations, knower of the lineage and family of samādhis; the body of samādhi, the supreme body, the king of all saṃbhogakāyas.

(146) The supreme body of the nirmāṇakāya, upholder of the Buddha’s lineage of emanations; manifesting as various forms throughout the ten directions, performing the welfare of the world according to its needs.
(147) God beyond gods, lord of gods, sovereign of the *suras*, lord of the *dānavas*; lord of the immortals, preceptor of the gods, destroyer, and lord of destroyers.
(148) One who has crossed the wilderness of existence, the sole Teacher, the Guru of the world, renowned throughout the worlds of the ten directions as the great Lord of the Gift of Dharma;

(149) Girt with the armor of loving-kindness (*maitrī*), clad in the mail of compassion (*karuṇā*), bearing the sword of wisdom (*prajñā*) and the bow and arrows; the destroyer of the enemies of afflictions and the objects of cognition (*jñeya*); (150) The enemy of Māra, the conqueror of Māra, the hero who brings an end to the fear of the four Māras, the victor over all the armies of Māra—the Perfectly Awakened One (*sambuddha*), the Leader of the World.

(151) He is to be saluted, worshipped, greeted, and honored perpetually; he is most worthy of adoration, venerable, and the supreme teacher to whom one should bow. (152) His stride traverses the three worlds alone; his prowess extends to the limits of space; he possesses the three types of knowledge, is learned in the Vedas, purified, endowed with the six supernormal powers, and possessed of the six recollections. (153) The foremost among those to be awakened.
The foremost of awakenings;
the six syllables;
the hundred syllables.
He who holds the drop of the half-moon within the half of the half of the [circle] of all aspects.
One who knows the [proper] time;
one who upholds the lineage;
the foremost among those whose bodies are the body of meditative concentration.
The supreme body among embodied beings; the foremost of the *nirmāṇakāya*; the emanation body, the god beyond gods (*devātideva*) among bodies.
The Lord of Gods, the Lord of Asuras,
who has transcended existence—
the sole Teacher.
Famous throughout the ten directions,
girded with armor.
The arrow of the dharma of compassion;
[the arrow] of afflictions and knowledge.

The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is as limitless as space, transcendent of the world, and possessed of great supernatural power (*maharddhika*). Having reached the culmination of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), he has attained the true nature of wisdom (*prajñātattvatva*).

(154) He knows himself and knows others; he is all-knowing, for he is the supreme person (*agrapudgala*). Having transcended all comparisons, he is to be known as the supreme Lord of Knowledge (*jñānādhipa*).

He is the preeminent Lord of the Gift of Dharma (*dharmadānapati*), the teacher of the meaning of the four seals (*caturmudrā*), and the most worthy of veneration by those in the world who proceed toward the three vehicles of liberation (*niryāṇatraya*).
The Great Mañjuśrī, glorious and pure in the ultimate sense, fortunate throughout the three worlds, the bringer of all prosperity, the illustrious one, the best among the glorious;
[these are] the fifteen verses on the knowledge of the performance of duties.
Homage to you, the giver of boons, the foremost of Vajras; homage be to you, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi).
Homage to you, whose essence is emptiness; homage be to you, the awakening of the Buddhas!

Homage be to you, the passion of the Buddhas; homage again and again to you, the desire of the Buddhas! Homage to you, the joy of the Buddhas; homage again and again to you, the delight of the Buddhas! Homage to you, the smile of the Buddhas; homage again and again to you, the laughter of the Buddhas! Homage be to you, the speech of the Buddhas; homage again and again to you, the nature of the Buddhas!

Homage to you, the source of non-existence; homage to you, the source of the Buddhas. Homage to you, the source of space; homage to you, the source of primordial wisdom. Homage to you, the net of illusion; homage to you, the dance of the Buddhas. Homage to you, O All; homage to all of you; homage be to you, the Body of Wisdom. These are the five verses of praise for the wisdom of the five Tathāgatas.

O Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, this is that *Nāmasamgīti*, the unique and utterly pure recitation of the names of Mañjuśrī-jñānasattva—the wisdom-body of all Tathāgatas and the wisdom-form of the Blessed One.
It is for the purpose of generating in you unsurpassed joy, serene faith, and great exultation; for the purification of the secrets of body, speech, and mind;
and for the fulfillment and purification of the accumulations of merit and wisdom on the stages and perfections that have not yet been fully completed or purified.
For the sake of attaining the unsurpassed goal not yet attained,
for the sake of reaching what has not been reached,

and for the sake of upholding the guidance of the true Dharma of all Tathāgatas— this [teaching] has been taught, proclaimed, explained, analyzed, clarified, and empowered by me, O Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, through the empowerment of the reality-nature (dharmatā) of all mantras within your own continuum.
This is the praise of the first wheel; these are its eleven verses.

Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, this *Nāmasamgīti* is the secret of the body, speech, and mind of the perfectly pure and immaculate omniscient gnosis-body of all Tathāgatas; it is the awakening of the Buddhas, the realization of the Perfectly Enlightened Ones, and the unsurpassed state of all Tathāgatas.
It is the course of the *dharmadhātu* of all Sugatas.

It is the defeat of all the forces of Māra for the Victors; it is the power of the ten powers for those possessed of the ten powers; it is omniscience for the Omniscient One; it is the source of all the knowledges of the Omniscient One;
and it is the realization of all the Buddha-dharmas of all Buddhas.
It is the fulfillment of the accumulations of merit and wisdom, which are stainless and perfectly pure; it is the source of all great bodhisattvas and the field for all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas;
it is the realm of all prosperity among gods and humans;
and it is the foundation of the Mahāyāna.
It is the source of the bodhisattva’s conduct,
the culmination of the noble path,
and the touchstone for the liberations.
It is the arising of the path of definitive emergence;

The penetration of emptiness is the accomplishment for those devoted to the cultivation of the penetration of non-duality;

Abiding in the dwelling of the universal gate through both resolute conviction and mental attention to reality, he is endowed with a faith that penetrates all phenomena, which is supreme, untroubled, and permeated by wisdom; as he dwells thus throughout the three times and beyond time, all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, having gathered together again and again, will reveal to him the gates of all dharmas.

Furthermore, Brahmā, Indra, Upendra, Rudra, Nārāyaṇa, Sanatkumāra, Maheśvara, Kārttikeya, Mahākāla, Nandikeśvara, Yama, Varuṇa, Kuvera, Hārīti, and the World-Protectors (*lokapāla*) of the ten directions will constantly and continuously—day and night—provide supreme protection, defense, and guardianship in every way, at all times, and by every means, whether he is walking, standing, lying down, sitting, sleeping, waking, in meditative concentration (*samāhita*), or not in concentration; whether he is alone or in the midst of a great crowd; up to when he is in the midst of villages, towns, cities, districts, kingdoms, and royal capitals; up to when he is in the midst of Indra’s pillars, streets, lanes, city gates, market roads, crossroads, junctions, inner-city markets, and shops; up to when he has gone to empty houses, mountain caves, river valleys, or dense forests; and whether he is eating leftovers or not, intoxicated or heedless. Day and night, they will provide supreme auspiciousness.

And whatever other gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans there may be; and whatever other lords of the planets, constellations, and hosts of mothers; and whatever the seven mothers; and whatever yakṣiṇīs, rākṣasīs, and piśācīs—may they all, united, assembled, with their armies and retinues, provide protection, defense, and guardianship.
Furthermore, they shall infuse vigor and strength into his body.

They will bestow health, strength, and the increase of lifespan. This is the benefit of the fourth wheel; its verses are nineteen. Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, whoever shall daily recite this *Nāmasamgīti*, the crest-jewel of names, three times with unbroken commitment until it is committed to memory, or who, having it in a book, shall read and propagate it—

Taking as his object the form of the Blessed One, Mañjuśrī-jñānasattva, reflecting upon it and meditating deeply on that form, that great being will, before long, behold him by means of his form-body (*rūpakāya*) according to the Dharma and Vinaya; he will also behold all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas situated in the expanse of the sky, accompanied by various manifested form-bodies. For that great being, there shall never, at any time, or in any way, be a falling into the miserable states or lower realms, nor shall there be rebirth in a low family.
He will not be born in a border region; he will not have impaired faculties;
he will not have deficient faculties;
and he will not be born into a family of wrong views.
He will not be reborn in Buddha-fields where no Buddhas have appeared.
He will never be turned away from or remain ignorant of the appearance of a Buddha and the Dharma taught by him. Nor will he be reborn among the long-lived gods.

Nor will he be reborn during the intermediate kalpas of famine, disease, and weapons; nor will he be reborn during the times of the five corruptions (pañcakaṣāya). There shall be no fear of kings, enemies, or thieves;
nor shall there be any fear of total deprivation, poverty, or misfortune, nor any fear of ill-repute, slander, censure, infamy, or disgrace.
He will be endowed with a noble birth, family, and lineage.

He will be possessed of a form and complexion that are universally pleasing; he will be dear to the world, agreeable, pleasant to dwell with, and lovely to behold; and his speech will be auspicious, fortunate, and persuasive for sentient beings.
It will come to pass.

Wherever he is reborn, in every birth he will be one who remembers his former lives; he will possess great wealth and a great retinue, and his wealth and retinue will be inexhaustible. He will become a leader among all beings, endowed with the foremost virtues.
By nature, he will be endowed with the qualities of the six perfections;
he will dwell in the four divine abodes;
and he will be endowed with mindfulness, clear comprehension, skillful means, power, aspiration, and wisdom.
He will become an expert in all treatises and an eloquent speaker.
He will possess clear speech, be free from dullness, and have a sharp intellect.
He will be skillful, not indolent, contented, highly prosperous, and free from craving.
He will become one who inspires the utmost confidence in all sentient beings and will be esteemed by his preceptors, instructors, and gurus.
Furthermore, he will master arts and crafts (*śilpakalā*) previously unheard of.

He will be honored as a teacher and guru; this is the fifty-first benefit of the fifth wheel. Thus, O Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, such a practitioner who engages in the conduct of the mantra gateway will be endowed with immeasurable qualities.
And he will be endowed with other immeasurable qualities of this kind and this nature.

O Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, this bull among men who upholds the *Paramārthanāmasamgīti* will, before long, having fully accumulated the provisions of merit and wisdom, very swiftly perfect the qualities of a Buddha and awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.

Possessing the dharma of no small parinirvāṇa, he will be the teacher of the unsurpassed dharma for all sentient beings, empowered as the King of Dharma, whose drum of the true dharma resounds throughout the ten directions.

The benefits of the sixth wheel are immeasurable. *Oṃ sarvadharmābhāvasvabhāvaviśuddhavajra a a am aḥ prakṛtipariśuddhaḥ sarvadharma yad uta sarvatathāgatajñānakāyamañjuśrīpariśuddhitām upādāya*—thus, *a āḥ sarvatathāgatahṛdayam hara hara*. *Oṃ hūṃ hrīḥ bhagavan jñānamūrtivāgiśvara mahāvāca sarvadharmagaganāmalasupariśuddhadharmadhātujñānagarbha āḥ*. This is the placement of the mantra (*mantravinyāsa*). Then the glorious Vajradhara, his heart satisfied, with palms joined in reverence, bowed to the Protector, the Fully Awakened One, the Blessed Tathāgata. Together with many other lords, the Indras of Secrets who hold the vajra, and the Kings of Wrath, he spoke these words aloud: "We rejoice, O Protector! Excellent, excellent is this well-spoken [teaching]. A great benefit has been wrought for us, which leads to the attainment of Perfect Awakening. For the world that is without a protector and yearns for the fruit of liberation, this pure path to excellence has been proclaimed through the method of the Net of Illusion (*Māyājāla*). Profound, vast, and extensive, of great significance, it accomplishes the welfare of the world. This is indeed the domain of the Buddhas, taught by the Perfectly Awakened One. These are the five concluding verses. Thus ends the *Bhagavat-mañjuśrījñānasattva-paramārthanāmasaṃgīti*, spoken by the Blessed Tathāgata Śākyamuni from the chapter on the Net of Samādhis within the *Ārya-māyājāla*, the Great Yoga Tantra in sixteen thousand [verses].
